liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Shakedown Street** (1 review): Garcia flubbed the lyrics, but then the jam runs about 23 minutes, the longest Shakedown the reviewer has heard [32]
- **Peggy-O** (1 review): Reviewer calls Peggy-O mint condition, and singles out Ramble On Rose and Looks Like Rain in a strong first set [32]
- **Playin' In The Band** (1 review): Phil pressed his head against his monitor during the feedback and space-out section; Phil married Jill the next day [36]

## Setlist highlights

- **gd84-10-11 s1t01 Crowd**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [38]
- **gd84-10-11 s1t02 Shakedown Street**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [38]
- **gd84-10-11 s1t03 Greatest Story Ever Told**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [38]
- **gd84-10-11 s1t04 Peggy O**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [38]
- **gd84-10-11 s1t05 Mama Tried**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [38]
- **gd84-10-11 s1t06 Big River**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [38]
- **gd84-10-11 s1t07 Ramble On Rose**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [38]
- **gd84-10-11 s1t08 Looks Like Rain**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [38]

## The recordings

- **gd1984-10-11.143631.nak.blend.guy.miller.clugston.flac1648** (recommended): audience recording; 21 songs; 150 min; rated 4/5 by 1 [1]
- **gd1984-10-11.beyerm160.mccabe.ladner.33825.sbeok.flac16**: audience recording; 20 songs; 141 min [3]
- **gd1984-10-11.fob.senn441.andrewf.94404.sbeok.flac16**: audience recording; 19 songs; 151 min; rated 4.5/5 by 2 [8]
- **gd1984-10-11.schoeps.oade.sacks.8794.sbefail.shnf**: source not stated; 19 songs; 148 min; rated 4.75/5 by 4 [12]. Said about its sound: Recording sounds intimate, like the band is in your living room, with strong bass on the opener, Women and Playin' jam [37]
- **gd84-10-11.oade.sacks.17411.sbeok.shnf**: source not stated; 19 songs; 148 min; rated 4.27/5 by 15 [14]. Said about its sound: Every musician is audible, with substantial bottom end and stage energy; better than some cold-sounding soundboards; Wide dynamic range: deep bass, crisp cymbals, wood-on-drum clack; Garcia's gravelly voice audible; warm but not muffled [29][33]

## Around the show

- Recalls a group backrub between sets, a small venue and very enthusiastic crowds on this night and the next [27]
- A hill beside the parking lot, with scattered trees, overlooked the Civic Center; fans camped there with a small fire and tents [30]
- Attended both Augusta nights; the scene and sound captured what the Dead were about [31]
- Fans drove eight hours from Oneonta, NY, leaving at 6am, in 70-80 degree weather, stopping by a river in Vermont [34]
- Reviewer judges the 12th the better show, though the 11th was solid; Garcia seemed to be at a low point [27]
- Says the 83-84 shows differed greatly from the late-80s shows they began attending in 88; small venue, Jerry playing hard [28]
- Reviewer likes this and the following night's download both, apparently preferring this one [33]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1984-10-11.143631.nak.blend.guy.miller.clugston.flac1648**: taped by Mike Guy; transferred by Scott Clugston and Charlie Miller; source: Mike Guy's Master Audience Cassettes; 3 mic spread - (2) Nakamichi CM300 mics w/ CP-4 shotgun caps + (1) Nakamichi CM100 mics w/CP-2 omni cap blend > Nakamichi… [1]
- **gd1984-10-11.beyerm160.mccabe.ladner.33825.sbeok.flac16**: taped by Derek McCabe; transferred by Chris Ladner; source: FOB Beyer M160s > Sony TCD5M > Master Audience Cassette (Maxell MX90 Type IV Cassettes) [3]. Also: Tape heads were cleaned and demagged, transferred at 24-bit/96kHz with Wavelab, then noise reduction applied before 16-bit rendering [3]
- **gd1984-10-11.fob.senn441.andrewf.94404.sbeok.flac16**: taped by Andrew F.; transferred by Andrew F.; source: FOB AUD: Sennhesier MD-441's > Sony TC-D5M > Maxell UD-XLII 90's, no Dolby. Mics on seven-foot stood, angled up at stacks, approx 25 feet from the stage, in… [8]. Also: Upgrade of the earlier 5304 audience recording, with patches from the 33825 and 17411 sources for Set 2 tuning and Playin' [8]
- **gd1984-10-11.schoeps.oade.sacks.8794.sbefail.shnf**: taped by Oade Brothers; transferred by Darrin Sacks; source: Oade Recording -- FOB -- Schoeps CMC 441> Oade M118 > Sony TC D5>DATs (@44.1k). [12]
- **gd84-10-11.oade.sacks.17411.sbeok.shnf**: source: Oade Recording -- FOB -- Schoeps CMC 441> Oade M118 > Sony TC D5>DATs (@44.1k). [14]

claims.text: Recalls a group backrub between sets, a small venue and very enthusiastic crowds on this night and the next
Reviewer judges the 12th the better show, though the 11th was solid; Garcia seemed to be at a low point
Says the 83-84 shows differed greatly from the late-80s shows they began attending in 88; small venue, Jerry playing hard
Every musician is audible, with substantial bottom end and stage energy; better than some cold-sounding soundboards
A hill beside the parking lot, with scattered trees, overlooked the Civic Center; fans camped there with a small fire and tents
Attended both Augusta nights; the scene and sound captured what the Dead were about
Garcia flubbed the lyrics, but then the jam runs about 23 minutes, the longest Shakedown the reviewer has heard
Reviewer calls Peggy-O mint condition, and singles out Ramble On Rose and Looks Like Rain in a strong first set
Wide dynamic range: deep bass, crisp cymbals, wood-on-drum clack; Garcia's gravelly voice audible; warm but not muffled
Reviewer likes this and the following night's download both, apparently preferring this one
Fans drove eight hours from Oneonta, NY, leaving at 6am, in 70-80 degree weather, stopping by a river in Vermont
Phil pressed his head against his monitor during the feedback and space-out section; Phil married Jill the next day
Recording sounds intimate, like the band is in your living room, with strong bass on the opener, Women and Playin' jam
Master audience cassette from Mike Guy, transferred by Charlie Miller; a Nakamichi CM100 source patches 14 seconds in Drums
Tape heads were cleaned and demagged, transferred at 24-bit/96kHz with Wavelab, then noise reduction applied before 16-bit rendering
Upgrade of the earlier 5304 audience recording, with patches from the 33825 and 17411 sources for Set 2 tuning and Playin'
